name: Number of edges in a pancyclic graph on n+2 vertices with the fewest possible edges.
comment: A graph on n vertices is said to be pancyclic if there are cycles of each length 3, 4, ... n in the graph.
link: Erdős problems database contributors, Erdős problem database, see no. 1016.
example: For n = 3 the answer is 3; each of the three vertices is connected to each other vertex, forming a 3-cycle. For n = 4 we find it takes five edges and for n = 5 it takes 6.
author: John C. George (jgeorge(AT)gdn.edu), Walter D. Wallis (wdwallis(AT)siu.edu) and _Alison Marr_, Apr 12 2005
